entertainment.title: Dancing With The Stars Finale Poll: Who Will Win Season 35? And Who Should?
entertainment.summary: Before Dancing With the Stars crowns its Season 35 winner on Tuesday, we want your thoughts on who will win the Mirrorball this time around - and who should.
entertainment.body:
ABC (5) Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover We'll be honest with you, "Dancing With the Stars" faithful: For the first time in a long time, we've got no idea who will take home that Mirrorball trophy.

Season 35 of the ABC reality competition wraps up with a three-hour finale on Tuesday, November 24 (8/7c), but after the surprising eliminations of frontrunners Jenna Dewan and Harry Shum Jr. , the race for the Mirrorball is wide open. Think an Olympic athlete has it in the bag? Well, here come dark horse Maura Higgins, fan favorite Tatyana Ali, and lovable underdog Connor Wood to shake up those assumptions ( and Kalshi bets ).

Ahead of Tuesday's season ender, we want your thoughts on not only who will win the latest "Dancing" season, but who should win it. Let's take stock of the remaining contestants before you cast your votes in our polls.

ABC On paper, at least, there are two couples — Ezra Frech and Daniella Karagach and Amber Glenn and Pasha Pashkov — who seem in slightly closer proximity to that Mirrorball. Ezra, a Paralympic gold medalist and above-the-knee amputee, has stunned us from the start with his capabilities on the dance floor, especially in a Week 2 cha-cha that was as self-assured and well-synchronized as anything we would see in the finale rounds. Daniella, a fan-favorite pro who's never met a choreographing hurdle she couldn't jump, has come up with creative, adaptive routines for her partner all season long, and Ezra has risen to the challenge each week with an upbeat attitude and enthusiasm for feedback, all of which go a long way with voters. (See: Connor Wood, below.)

Similarly, Olympic figure skater Amber has been a dancing force since the early weeks of Season 35. Did we expect that a little, given her athletic background? Sure. Have we been any less impressed by her viral Super Bowl Night samba , her evocative Dedication Night contemporary , or her sultry semifinals Viennese waltz ? Not a bit. And though Ezra and Amber are pretty evenly matched in both skill and scores, Amber has the advantage of being paired with Pasha, a perennially underrated pro who has yet to win a Mirrorball, though he got close with Ariana Madix in Season 32. Longtime fans' desire to get Pasha an overdue victory could be the deciding factor here, if it's indeed down to Amber and Ezra in the Final Two.

But let's not overlook "The Traitors" alumni Maura Higgins and Mark Ballas , who have straddled the line between frontrunners and underdogs all season. I'd nudge them over to the frontrunner category, though, especially after Maura's big, unexpected breakout moment in the very first week of competition . Though she's had some weak performances (namely the contemporary and jive, both of which exposed floppy feet), she's bounced back nicely in these high-stakes final weeks of competition, giving us a terrific Argentine tango in Week 9 and back-to-back stunners (a samba and a Viennese waltz) in the semifinals. Voting-wise, it's unclear if Maura has the fanbase to compete with some of her fellow finalists, but her authentic personality has been endearing to many — and let's not forget there's still a Mark Ballas-choreographed freestyle coming our way. Maura's very much a contender, even if that would shock her nervous Week 1 self.

entertainment.title: Michael Douglas' First Leading Role On A TV Show Was In This Classic Crime Drama
entertainment.summary: Michael Douglas landed his big break as a San Francisco detective in a '70s TV crime drama that partnered him with Oscar winner Karl Malden.
entertainment.body:
During an interview with The Guardian , Douglas described "The Streets of San Francisco," saying, "It was the greatest opportunity I ever had, but also the hardest. We shot 14 hours a day, six days a week, for eight and a half months. I've never worked harder, but I learned so much about acting and producing."

Speaking to the Television Academy , Douglas also opened up about just how influential Malden was as a mentor. "He was renowned for his work ethic, and he set the tone for the show," Douglas recalled. He also noted their genuine off-screen bond: "We loved each other. He always told me, 'You're the son that I never had.'" Malden never hogged the spotlight, urging Douglas early on to take the front position on camera.

Today on IMDb , the show holds a solid 7.3 rating, but one thing fans agree on is that it just wasn't the same after Douglas left and was replaced by Richard Hatch, who played Inspector Dan Robbins. One user described the series as "good stories, well directed, thoughtful in short doses. Worth your time until Douglas exits, then it fades to black."

Another user agreed, writing that when Hatch became Malden's new partner, "they never quite got it together as a team the way Malden did with Douglas." The reviewer continued, "I liked the show, I liked the stories. But most of all Malden and Douglas were a joy to watch."

As for why Douglas left, he just couldn't resist the opportunity to attach himself as producer on a movie based on one of his favorite novels: "One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest." He told the Television Academy that while many thought he was "nuts" to abandon the show, both Malden and producer Quinn Martin gave their blessing. "Today, in television, nobody is going to let you out of your contract," Douglas said. "But both Quinn and Karl said, 'Absolutely. Go for it. We loved working with you.'" Douglas' instincts paid off. The film ended up scoring him an Academy Award for best picture, his first Oscar.

entertainment.title: 5 Cop Dramas From The '80s That Redefined The Genre
entertainment.summary: These cop dramas from the 1980s offered viewers a new take on the genre, becoming fan favorites almost immediately thanks to their unique perspectives.
entertainment.body:
NBC Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover The 1980s were an exciting time for cop shows. Television audiences were treated to some of the best new shows that pushed the envelope and secured a legacy that influenced cop shows today.

Up-close camera work and large casts of characters (as well as their intersecting storylines) are police drama aspects that audiences are not only familiar with, but can't get enough of. Because of this, many of the 1980s cop shows still hold up today , and their influence is still prominent in contemporary procedural dramas. Series like "Blue Bloods" and "The Rookie" would not be as popular as they are without the shows that came before, especially during such a monumental decade for television.

In the spirit of celebrating shows that walked the 1980s so others could run today, here is a list of 5 redefining cop shows from the decade. These are not the shows that simply entertained audiences, but introduced them to the true potential of the genre.

Developed by the legendary Steven Bochco, "Hill Street Blues" was groundbreaking for showcasing the personal lives of the officers without a black-and-white lens. The series explored a side of police work that television shied away from, such as urban decay and systemic oppression. It also utilized creative formats that weren't common for cop shows at the time, such as ensemble casts and its use of handheld cameras. This allowed viewers to feel like they were in the fast-paced action with the police characters.

Today, audiences are well accustomed to gritty, morally-grey police procedurals that don't just explore law enforcement, but the enforcers themselves. Shows like "The Wire," "The Shield," and others of the best police procedurals of all time owe their success at least partially to "Hill Street Blues."

NBC Cop shows like "T.J. Hooker" and "Miami Vice" utilized a "case of the week" format. They would generally begin and wrap up a storyline with each episode. NBC's "Crime Story" pivoted away from that.

Developed by Michael Mann, "Crime Story" centered on the long-standing feud between Chicago police lieutenant Mike Torello (Dennis Farina) and a mobster named Ray Luca (Anthony Denison). Initially set in the 1960s, the series followed the cat-and-mouse struggle between the two against the historical backdrop of the decades, including Luca's trek into Las Vegas casinos. The series also featured a plethora of established celebrity guest stars, and those who had yet to break out in the industry. This included the likes of Ving Rhames and Julia Roberts. Gary Sinise also starred on this groundbreaking crime drama .

entertainment.title: 10 Most Underrated Cartoon Network Shows Of All Time, Ranked
entertainment.summary: Cartoon Network has produced one legendary animated gem after another. Here are 10 of its shows that deserve far more recognition.
entertainment.body:
Cartoon Network Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover More than just licensing classic shows, Cartoon Network produced plenty of original series, both for its daytime programming and its late-night Adult Swim block. While we've celebrated the best Cartoon Network shows of all time , this time we're looking at the series on the cable channel that flew under the radar. From superhero shows to quirky sci-fi, there is no shortage of overlooked originals that just never quite found their wider audience. Each of the shows we're mentioning here are worthy of a reappraisal or at least more recognition than they got during their broadcast run.

Even shows featuring marquee licensed properties and produced by some of the most influential animators in the game struggled to land high viewership. Many of these shows are still available to stream on various platforms, each ripe for a revisit. It's a crowded market out there for animated series and each of these shows should've found greater success than they did. With that in mind, here are the 10 most underrated Cartoon Network shows of all time ranked to the most under-appreciated of them all.

Cartoon Network There's something endearing about the '70s educational animated series "Schoolhouse Rock," even if it wasn't originally meant to be on TV . The 2002 series "Whatever Happened to... Robot Jones?" subverts assumptions associated with that art style for its own nostalgic ends. The show is set in a Delaware suburb during the '80s where self-aware robots are relatively common and live among humans. Robot Jones (Bobby Block) tries to learn human behavior from his classmates as he attends a middle school and observes his friends.

Every episode of "Whatever Happened to... Robot Jones?" is divided up into a set of vignettes, each focusing on a different aspect of teenage behavior. Seeing Robot struggle to comprehend everything from skipping school to throwing a clandestine house party provides a steady amount of charm. The deliberately scratchy animation style and '80s setting gives the show a clear personality and sense of charm that makes it all the more appealing. In retrospect, "Whatever Happened to... Robot Jones?" may have worked better on Adult Swim instead of two seasons on Cartoon Network, but it still left an impression on us.

Cartoon Network Of all the shows to poke fun at the expected conventions of an animated series, "Sheep in the Big City" is the most surprising. Premiering in 2000, the show follows a nameless sheep (Kevin Seal) who escapes the farm to relocate to a bustling metropolis for a fresh start. This leads to him being pursued by both Farmer John (James Godwin) and the military as he embarks on nonsensical adventures. The series' format also keeps things delightfully inane, from a narrator (Ken Schatz) who complains about the bad writing to the inclusion of fake commercials.

entertainment.title: 50 Years Ago Today: The Beach Boys Play Pivotal ‘Brian’s Back’ Concert in Cincinnati
entertainment.summary: In the fall of 1976, the Beach Boys brought Brian back on the road for a tour that marked the last time the band played a significant amount of new material in concert
entertainment.body:
“Brian is the Beach Boys , and we’re his messengers,” Dennis Wilson told People magazine in its August 1976 cover story about the band. “We’re thrilled to have him back.”

Just a few years earlier, the idea of a 1960s has-been group appearing on the cover of a mainstream magazine like People would have seemed absurd, about as likely as Herman’s Hermits or the Dave Clark Five having a major resurgence. But the Beach Boys were the beneficiaries of an enormous nostalgia wave that swept America in the mid-1970s, giving us American Graffiti , Happy Days , Sha Na Na , and Grease .

The Beach Boys weren’t able to generate much interest in their new work, but their 1960s compilation Endless Summer hit Number One in October 1974. As a result, they dumped most of the recent material from their live repertoire and began playing arenas and even stadiums. “We knocked them dead every time we went out just playing the hits,” Al Jardine told Rolling Stone in 2025 . “It allowed us to grow musically at home while we could continue to entertain. It was a nice balance.”

But by 1976, as Endless Summer mania began petering out, the group needed a new gambit to keep drawing the big crowds. That’s why band manager Steve Love decided to rouse Brian Wilson from his bed and get him back on the road for the first time since 1964, generating a groundswell of interest in the band.

They promoted the “Brian’s Back” campaign with an NBC television special put together by Lorne Michaels and the original Saturday Night Live team, which included a legendary sketch where Dan Aykroyd and John Belushi storm into Brian’s bedroom as the “Surf Police” and force him to surf for the first time. Annie Leibovitz shot a classic photo of Wilson standing on the sand that day in his blue robe, which appeared on the Nov. 4, 1976, cover of Rolling Stone .

Much of the press outside of Rolling Stone presented Wilson as a goofy eccentric rather than a genuine genius. “Brian is like an amiable child (violence was never one of his symptoms) trying to relearn the simple social graces,” People wrote. “As Brian told Mike [Love] lately, ‘I’m tired of being a failure.'” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century

That’s why he decided not only to join the tour but also to produce a new Beach Boys record for the first time since Pet Sounds . The result was the underwhelming 15 Big Ones , which is thin on new originals and heavy on classic covers like Chuck Berry’s “Rock and Roll Music,” the Dixie Cups’ “Chapel of Love,” and Fats Domino’s “Blueberry Hill.”

entertainment.title: All 4 Lori Loughlin Hallmark Christmas Movies, Ranked
entertainment.summary: Lori Loughlin's holiday films for Hallmark feature a little romance, a few tired tropes, and a dash of real Christmas magic (including an appearance by Santa).
entertainment.body:
Hallmark Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Lori Loughlin is one of the most well-known faces on the Hallmark Channel thanks to her roles as Abigail Stanton on "When Calls the Heart" and Jennifer Shannon in the "Garage Sale Mysteries" franchise. "When Calls the Heart" has a few Christmas specials that Loughlin has been a part of, but surprisingly, before the college admissions scandal , the "Full House" star had only been in three Hallmark original Christmas movies outside of the world of Hope Valley.

Loughlin officially returned to Hallmark in a surprise appearance in the "When Calls the Heart" Season 13 finale. The "Fuller House" star will also appear in six episodes of the show in 2027 for Season 14 . She's further solidified her return to Hallmark in another "Garage Sale Mysteries" installment and her fourth Hallmark original Christmas movie, "What If Christmas." In the latter, Loughlin stars as a former fashion designer who sacrifices her career ambitions to support her husband's career in cardiac surgery. Tom Cavanagh also stars in the film, which aired in October 2026 as part of Hallmark's Countdown to Christmas" lineup .

"What If Christmas" now exists forever in Loughlin's filmography on the network and its streaming service, Hallmark+. So, we're ranking her Christmas films from worst to best to help you decide which of the four titles belongs in your movie lineup this holiday season. Loughlin plays an appraiser turned innkeeper, a shoe designer, a fashion designer, and a reporter in her respective Christmas journeys. And, even if a few of her characters' careers are similar, the lessons they learn are very different. So, get ready to make some hard choices.

Hallmark In "Homegrown Christmas," Lori Loughlin plays Maddie Finley, a shoe designer who has recently sold her Manhattan-based company and goes home for Christmas to figure out what she wants to do in the next phase of her life. Her ex-boyfriend Carter (Victor Webster) still works at her family's furniture workshop. So, they're bound to run into each other and bump up against memories from their relationship that they would both rather bury. But when Maddie's sister volunteers her to help plan the holiday dance the family promised to host for the community, they can no longer keep the promise they made to give each other space.

"Homegrown Christmas" isn't a bad film; it's just a very boring one. It uses the most basic trope in TV Christmas movies — the lead comes home from the big city to find herself and runs into her ex — and does absolutely nothing unique with it. Webster and Loughlin's chemistry isn't strong enough to carry that alone. There are subplots; Carter's niece Ava (played by Loughlin's oldest daughter Isabella Giannulli) wants to be a fashion designer and seeks mentorship from Maddie. Plus, Maddie's sister Hallie (Kate Craven) is rude about Maddie's attempts to bond with her after so much time away. But neither story is developed enough for the audience to emotionally invest in. "Homegrown Christmas" is a good choice to watch if you like background noise while wrapping presents but still need to focus.

entertainment.title: Stephen King Thought Haven's Original Pilot Script Was Too Loyal To His Book
entertainment.summary: The show Haven was inspired by Stephen King's book The Colorado Kid, but when King read the pilot script, he actually wanted it to be less like his novel.
entertainment.body:
So what did King think about the first pilot script for "Haven"? Inspired by King's novel "The Colorado Kid," the 2010 Syfy show follows an FBI agent uncovering the truth behind residents in a coastal town suffering from a mysterious curse. Unfortunately, the popular author wasn't initially pleased when he read the pilot for "Haven," because he felt that it stuck too closely to his story. "Initially, our idea was to stay close to the book. So it had no supernatural element," explained co-creator Sam Ernst to The Philadelphia Inquirer ahead of the show's premiere. "But when King read it, the first thing he said was, 'Where's the supernatural element?'"

At King's urging, they changed the trajectory of the sci-fi show , shifting the plot so that someone with a new supernatural affliction was added each week.

Syfy Stephen King wasn't initially sold on the pilot for "Haven," but he was incredibly supportive of the project once things got going, according to "Haven" producer Shawn Piller. In 2010, Piller spoke about how King had decided to back this particular TV adaptation of his work. "He's approved every step along the way," Piller told TV Squad (via Digital Spy ). "If you're offending a writer, you're doing something they wouldn't do. And if you're p***sing off the writer, the fans aren't going to like it." Ultimately, "Haven" aired for five seasons, and it has a 7.5 average rating on IMDb , so it obviously found favor with its audience.

Even with the initial pushback, "Haven" fared better with King than some of his other adaptations. For example, King is much fonder of the TV adaptation of his novel "The Shining" than the film directed by Stanley Kubrick, and he doesn't mind who knows. "I dislike the film," King told The New York Times in 2020. "... I admire the film, and I admire Kubrick as a director, which sometimes gets lost in the mix when people who absolutely love that film take me to task. I love Kubrick as a filmmaker, but I just felt that he didn't have the chops for this particular thing."

entertainment.body:
Tommy Lee Jones is discussing his decision to live on a ranch in his Texas hometown and one of his hobbies that has carried over since the ’70s.

During a recent interview with The New York Times , the 80-year-old actor shared how he decided to move back to San Saba, Texas, in the early 2000s, saying, “I knew that God loved me because he put me on the ground in Texas.”

“There came a time when I became aware that I could live anywhere I wanted to,” Jones said. “So, in my wisdom, I went home.”

The actor now lives on a 6,000-acre ranch in a two-story home originally built in 1856 and has turned it into the home he always wanted, noting he wanted to live somewhere that didn’t have “any fences around the house.”

When speaking to the outlet, the “No Country for Old Men” star shared that living on the ranch also allowed him to enjoy playing polo. The actor grew up riding horses and began playing polo in the 1970s.

Since moving onto his ranch, Jones has built two polo fields on the property, which now also holds 25 horses, and the actor and his wife, Dawn Laurel-Jones, host many polo events throughout the year.

Although Jones doesn’t compete anymore, his wife continues to participate in competitions.

“She’s one of the better female polo players in the United States,” Jones said of his wife.

entertainment.title: HGTV star Ty Pennington calls out ‘excessive’ home renovation trend people do in kitchens
entertainment.summary: The reality star weighed in on where homeowners should and shouldn't put their renovation budgets.
entertainment.body:
Ty Pennington has built and maintained a successful career with his extreme home makeovers, but there’s one renovation trend he believes homeowners are taking a little too far these days.

In an exclusive interview with Fox News Digital, Pennington — who has recently partnered with Insmed on the “Suspect BE” campaign to encourage people with unresolved respiratory symptoms to pursue further testing — weighed in on where homeowners should and shouldn’t put their renovation budgets, calling out oversized kitchen islands packed with redundant appliances as a trend that has crossed into overkill.

“I would probably say the island with three dishwashers,” the veteran HGTV star, 62, said when asked about renovation trends that go overboard. “It’s maybe a little excessive. This is coming from somebody who was a personal dishwasher for many years of my life.”

“There is a point that you almost get too big,” he continued.

“Is there an island that’s almost the size of a small court? Possible. So I think sometimes we may be sort of outgrowing things. We may be just going too big. I know that’s hard to believe, but I think sometimes we’ve got to scale back not only in budget, but also maybe in size. Cozy is cool.”

While Pennington advocates for dialing back the scale, he still acknowledges that kitchens and bathrooms remain the smartest investments for homeowners looking to build equity.

“The most expensive are the kitchens and the bathrooms, but I do think they’re kind of necessary if you plan on selling, because that’s what people look at first,” he explained.

When tackling home projects and renovation with his wife, Kellee Merrell, Pennington said compromise can prevent them from budding heads.

entertainment.title: Quote Of The Day By Carol Burnett: 'When I Lost My Daughter Carrie I Really Didn't Want To Get Out Of Bed. She And...'
entertainment.summary: The comedy icon lost her daughter to cancer in the early 2000s and had to learn how to manage the sadness.
entertainment.body:
In 2024, Burnett received a historic Emmy nomination for her supporting role "Palm Royale," becoming the oldest female nominee ever in her category. Although she didn't win for that performance, over the course of her career, she won seven other Emmys. Burnett also received both a SAG and Golden Globes' lifetime achievement award for her contributions to the comedy scene.

With a sense of humor comparable to Lucille Ball's (her co-star in "The Lucy Show") and a grounded presence that made her roles in "Better Call Saul" and "Glee" hard to forget, Burnett has nothing left to prove. At 93, the actor is satisfied with what she's achieved and doesn't pressure herself to reach EGOT status (even though she is an Oscar away from getting it).

Burnett's lighthearted approach to her professional and personal life is largely informed by her late daughter, Carrie Hamilton. She died of cancer in 2002, and throughout her health battle, she never let go of her optimism. The quote of the day shows how Hamilton still impacts Burnett to this day.

TVLine "When I lost my daughter Carrie, I really didn't want to get out of bed. She and I had been writing a play, and it wasn't finished yet."

The quote above comes from an interview that Carol Burnett did with Fox News in 2015. In it, the actor discussed her role in paving the way for women in sketch and the ways in which she remains strong following the loss of her daughter.

Carrie Hamilton was an actor and playwright, and she and Burnett were collaborating on a Broadway production called "Hollywood Arms," which was based on the latter's memoir. Yet, Hamilton passed away before they finished writing it together.

Burnett wrote the rest of the play on her own, and although she was struggling, "Hollywood Arms" became an outlet to deal with the pain. "It's been 14 years. You never get over it, but you learn to cope," she added.

In the same interview with Fox News, the comedian remembered an instance before Carrie Hamilton's death where a nurse approached her to say that she was surprised by Hamilton's optimism while in the hospital. "The nurse said, 'She's always so cheerful and smiling, and I asked her how can she be smiling?' Carrie told the nurse, 'I'm going to decide to love my life today.' So I do that."

entertainment.title: Britney Spears Apologizes to Her Family on Instagram: ‘I Just Miss Them Like Crazy’
entertainment.summary: The pop star wrote that she regretted raising past grievances publicly, five years after the end of the conservatorship that fractured her relationship with her parents and sister.
entertainment.body:
Britney Spears posted a public apology to her family on Saturday (Nov. 21), writing on Instagram that she regretted revisiting past conflicts in public.

“I’m so very sorry for bringing up past issues, but I think I did because I realized I needed to protect my heart,” Spears wrote. “It’s the way I love, and when I love you, I really love you.” Related Miley Cyrus Marries Maxx Morando in Poolside Ceremony Led by the Flaming Lips' Wayne Coyne Gorillaz Celebrate Mexico's 'Revolutionary Spirit' at Corona Capital, Bring Out Johnny Marr and Trueno BTS, ENHYPEN, BIGBANG & CORTIS Are Big Winners of 2026 MAMA Awards Explore Britney Spears See latest videos, charts and news

She described her own conduct as “childish and embarrassing,” adding: “Thoughts on the past, I’m obviously human, and there actually might be something to those things I said psychology-wise; either way, I’m sorry to my family for bringing up those memories.”

Spears said the conversation had never taken place directly. “I’ve never actually spoken to them face to face on it,” she wrote. “I just miss them like crazy! And I’m very sorry!” She also called herself “blessed to have such a beautiful family.”

Spears is the eldest child of Jamie and Lynne Spears, who are divorced. She has a brother, Bryan, and a sister, Jamie Lynn Spears .

The relationship has been publicly strained for years. Spears spent 13 years under a conservatorship, established in February 2008 with her father as conservator, which gave others control over her finances, career and personal decisions. After an explosive court hearing in June 2021 in which she testified against the arrangement, a Los Angeles judge suspended Jamie Spears that September and terminated the conservatorship on Nov. 12, 2021.

In the years since, Spears has repeatedly addressed the fallout. “Honestly my family embarrassed me and hurt me deeply,” she wrote in December 2021, a month after the termination. Her 2023 memoir The Woman in Me detailed her account of the arrangement, including her view that it “stripped me of my womanhood, made me into a child,” and addressed tensions with her sister.

The sisters’ relationship had already become public: Spears sent Jamie Lynn a cease and desist letter in early 2022 over claims in her sibling’s memoir Things I Should Have Said , published two months after the conservatorship ended. The pair appeared to move toward reconciliation in mid-2023, when Spears posted about visiting the set of Jamie Lynn’s film Zoey 102 .

entertainment.title: Miley Cyrus Marries Maxx Morando in Poolside Ceremony Led by the Flaming Lips’ Wayne Coyne
entertainment.summary: It comes one month after the couple performed “Let’s Get Married” together at the Hollywood Bowl.
entertainment.body:
Miley Cyrus married Maxx Morando on Saturday (Nov. 21) in a poolside ceremony in Palm Springs, Calif., with the Flaming Lips ’ Wayne Coyne officiating, one month after the couple sang “Let’s Get Married” together on the Hollywood Bowl stage. Explore Miley Cyrus See latest videos, charts and news

Coyne, who worked with Cyrus on her 2015 album Miley Cyrus & Her Dead Petz and joined her onstage at the Hollywood Bowl in October, led the vows as Cyrus, 33, and Morando, 28, stood beneath an arch of white flowers in front of family and friends, according to photos published by People . Cyrus wore a long-sleeved white satin gown with a high neck, open back and small train, and was photographed wiping away tears during the vows, while Morando wore a black suit. Related Gorillaz Celebrate Mexico's 'Revolutionary Spirit' at Corona Capital, Bring Out Johnny Marr and Trueno BTS, ENHYPEN, BIGBANG & CORTIS Are Big Winners of 2026 MAMA Awards Ariana Grande Recalls 'Wildest Place' She's Heard Her Music Playing: 'Getting a Bikini Wax'

Among the guests were her mother, Tish Cyrus, and husband Dominic Purcell; her sister Noah Cyrus ; and her father, Billy Ray Cyrus , along with Elizabeth Hurley. The celebrations began the night before with a rehearsal dinner, glimpsed in Instagram photos posted by Cyrus’ stepsister Lily-Rose Purcell that showed tables dressed with dark red flowers and small candles, and a menu topped with an “M+M” monogram.

The wedding caps a year in which the relationship moved from the edges of Cyrus’ public life to the center of her work. “Let’s Get Married,” which Morando co-wrote and co-produced, appears on Bass Persuades , her 10th studio album and her first released simply as Miley. Its black-and-white video, directed by Mert Alas and shot at West Hollywood’s Chateau Marmont, casts Morando opposite her — a dress rehearsal, as it turned out, for the real thing two months later.

That album also brought Cyrus back to the top of the Billboard 200, debuting at No. 1 on the chart dated Oct. 3 with 61,000 equivalent album units, according to Luminate. It gave her a sixth No. 1 album and her first since Bangerz in 2013.

It marks a striking shift for a couple who spent years largely out of view. Morando, the drummer for Los Angeles rock band Liily, was first linked to Cyrus in late 2021, when the pair attended a Gucci event together. The two had been set up on a blind date — “Well, it was blind for me and not really for him,” she told British Vogue in 2023 — and he later joined her at the 2024 Grammy Awards, where “Flowers” won record of the year. Morando proposed in October 2025 in a garden on the grounds of their hotel in Kyoto, Japan, telling Wonderland he held out “until the very last moment of the very last day” to keep it a surprise. The engagement went public in early December 2025, when Cyrus wore the ring to the Dec. 1 premiere of Avatar: Fire and Ash in Los Angeles.

sports.title: Bills can match their best record through 10 games, with a win over Dolphins
sports.summary: The 8-1 Bills, barring a massive upset, will move to 9-1 today.
sports.body:
Via NBC Sports research, the Bills have started 9-1 four prior times. Most recently, it happened in 1991. (They lost the Super Bowl that year.) It also occurred in 1990. (They lost the Super Bowl that year, too.)

It also happened in 1988, when they eventually lost in the AFC Championship to the Bengals. The first time the Bills started 9-1 was in 1964, when they won the AFL Championship.

Beyond the 16.5-point spread, the Dolphins are an ideal opponent. Buffalo has beaten Miami at home 10 times in a row. It’s the Bills’ longest winning streak at home against any team in franchise history.

The creampuff portion of the schedule ends today for the Bills. On Thursday night, they host the Chiefs. After what should be an easy win over the quarterback-less Patriots, the Bills visit the Packers, host the Bears, and visit the Broncos.

Today’s game is an important one for both clubs, but the Bills have very different goals. Buffalo will look to improve on its 1-1 record v
sports.body: It’s finally time, Rumblers! The Buffalo Bills get their first crack at the Miami Dolphins today, and the two teams couldn’t be much further apart if they tried. Today’s game is an important one for both clubs, but the Bills have very different goals. Buffalo will look to improve on its 1-1 record versus the AFC East, and to maintain sole possession of first place in the AFC. Miami is looking to build upon its first victory last Sunday, and winning against the conference-leading Bills would go a long way in building confidence for the rebuilding team. Buffalo will have to rely on quite a few backups today based on the Bills’ Week 11 inactive list. Starters in cornerback Christian Benford and inside linebacker Dorian Williams were ruled out Friday afternoon. The Bills will also be without starting tight end Dalton Kincaid, whose prior “doubtful” game-day designation now turns into “out” for Week 11. Despite showing up as “questionable” due to a late injury on Saturday, defensive tackle Ed Oliver is not among Buffalo’s inactive players. We’ll see how much he’s able to contribute this afternoon. Make no mistake, this is a very important game for the Bills despite the circumstances of their opponent. Buffalo will have a short week of rest and to prepare for their Week 12 opponents, the Kansas City Chiefs, who they host in primetime on Thanksgiving night. Will head coach Joe Brady and the Bills’ offense look to feature the ground-and-pound rushing attack today, in an effort to shorten the game and wear down Miami? It’s work well in recent weeks against other opponents, and running back James Cook III has a goal to hit 2,000 yards on the ground this season. With that all in mind, here’s your open thread for Bills-Dolphins in Week 11. As always, be kind to one another — and in all things… Go Bills!

sports.title: Colts rejected a trade offer from the Ravens for Daniel Jones
sports.summary: Ten days after the November 10 trade deadline, the Colts cut quarterback Daniel Jones.
sports.body:
Per ESPNFL, the Ravens would have sent a fourth-round pick to the Colts for Jones and a fifth-round pick. The Colts would have gotten their fifth-round pick back if the Ravens had made it to the playoffs.

The Vikings, per the report, were talking to the Colts about Jones but never made an offer. (That doesn’t mean, obviously, that two teams didn’t speak in terms about what it would take to get Jones. If anything, the possibility of getting Jones for less than a third-round pick may have helped the Vikings get Kirk Cousins from the Raiders for only a third-round pick.)

Obviously, the Colts should have taken the offer. They cut him after only two more games — a win over the Dolphins and a loss to the Texans. (Compensatory draft picks aren’t available when a player is released.)

Some will say that the Colts shouldn’t have dumped Jones for whatever they could get because he was still the starter. But the Colts knew (or should have known) what was coming. Eventually, Jones was going to be benched in order to ensure that he won’t suffer an injury that locked in his $10.51 million guarantee for 2027. (It was mentioned before the trade deadline .)

So the choices were obvious. Trade him and get something or keep him and get nothing.

Given the various ill-advised decisions the Colts have made since trading for cornerback Sauce Gardner last November, this one isn’t as glaring. But it’s still another unforced error by the Colts, fueled by a lack of vision and strategic planning.

sports.body: Something strange happened here at Buffalo Rumblings following the Buffalo Bills’ win against the New York Jets. It was the team’s first win against an AFC East foe this season (now 1-1), and the victory allowed them to retain their lead in the AFC playoff race thanks to an 8-1 overall record. Yet for some reason, there was a drop in confidence among some Rumblers who responded to our latest poll. Heading into the game versus the Jets, fan confidence was at 94%. A week later, just ahead of a home game with the Miami Dolphins, that confidence number has dropped to 89%. I blame the quality of opponent, rather than the way in which the Bills won. After all, winning, no matter how it looks, is the only thing that matters in the NFL. [Image: https://platform.buffalorumblings.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/51/2026/11/Bills_1_111626.png?quality=90&strip=all] I’m left wondering if it’s the situation in the rest of the AFC that has some in Bills Mafia concerned about the season. There are four other teams that remain serious threats to Buffalo’s one-seed goal. We asked readers about that this week, wondering which AFC team is the biggest threat to the Bills’ hopes of securing a playoff bye. I think recency bias prevail here in the results. Leading the way are the Cincinnati Bengals (43%), a team that doesn’t face Buffalo in the regular season. In second with 39% of the vote are the Jacksonville Jaguars — another team the Bills don’t face in the current regular season. There’s a precipitous drop after those teams, surprisingly. Just 10% of people saying that the Kansas City Chiefs are the biggest threat to Buffalo. Meanwhile, only 8% of those polled say the Broncos remain the Bills’ biggest challengers to the one seed. Why do I find surprise in these results? Yes, the Bengals and Jaguars are red-hot right now. Yet, I wonder if some people thought about the direct threat the Chiefs and Broncos represent to the Bills. Remember, Buffalo will face Kansas City (at home) on (equally) short rest/prep for Week 12. They play a road game at the Denver Broncos in Week 16, another major U.S. holiday. The Chiefs and Broncos have already played each other twice in 2026, splitting the series 1-1, which means there’s no longer a chance either team can acutely unseat the other before the playoffs. sports.title: Micah Parsons to practice in pads on Sunday
sports.summary: The Packers plan to have defensive end Micah Parsons on the field against the Rams on Wednesday night and Parsons will check off one more box toward that return to action at practice on Sunday.
sports.body:
Head coach Matt LaFleur told reporters at a press conference that Parsons will practice in pads for the first time since he got back on the practice field earlier this month. LaFleur called it “the next marker” for Parsons to clear before he gets the green light to face the Rams.

LaFleur said the team will have a plan in place for how many snaps Parsons would play in his first game since tearing his ACL last December.

“He is an elite player, he’s an elite athlete. I do think you see with many of these guys — I never want to put limitations on anybody, but he hasn’t played football in a long time. You gotta be conscious of that.”

The Packers will release their first injury report for Week 12 later on Sunday and injury designations for the NFL’s first Thanksgiving Eve game will be released on Tuesday.

sports.body: The New York Jets activated veteran wide receiver Sterling Shepard from the practice squad ahead of their game against the Los Angeles Chargers. Rookie receiver Omar Cooper Jr. is out for today’s game with an ankle injury, leaving the Jets short at wide receiver. Sterling Shepard is a 33 year old, 5’ 10”, 195 pound wide receiver. He was originally drafted out of Oklahoma by the New York Giants with the 40th overall pick in the 2nd round of the 2016 NFL draft. Shepard was an effective receiver for the Giants early in his career. He spent the first eight years of his career with the Giants before moving on after the 2023 season. Shepard played with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2024 and 2025 before being signed as an unrestricted free agent by the Jets in 2026. Sterling Shepard has been elevated to the active roster twice this season before today. He has been targeted twice by the Jets, with one reception good for three yards. The Jets needed another body at wide receiver with Cooper out. The team has Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell active, but behind those two are Tim Patrick and Malik McClain, who are unlikely to provide much value. Unfortunately, Shepard likely has little left to offer the Jets. He will turn 34 years old in February. Shepard has not exceeded 400 receiving yards in a season, a 50% success rate, or 7 yards per target since all the way back in 2020. The Jets might be better off giving practice squad receiver Jamaal Pritchett a shot. Pritchett has excelled each of the last two training camps, only to be buried on the practice squad in the regular season. Regardless of whether the Jets elevated Shepard or Pritchett, they will be thin at wide receiver until Cooper makes it back. In the meantime, who knows, maybe Shepard has a turn back the clock performance left in his tank.

sports.title: Broncos, TV legend Tom Jackson dies at 75
sports.summary: Tom Jackson, a 14-year veteran with the Broncos and a longtime fixture on ESPN's NFL programming, has died.
sports.body:
Jackson was a fourth-round pick of the Broncos in 1973. He became a full-time starter in his second season. He started a run of three straight Pro Bowl berths in 1977, the same year the Broncos made their first Super Bowl appearance.

Jackson played until 1986. The next year, he debuted on ESPN. He worked on the network’s Sunday NFL Countdown show and the must-see NFL Primetime , which featured extended highlights packages years before the best plays could be instantly seen on social media.

“All of us are stunned,” Jackson’s long-time on-air partner, Chris Berman, said in a statement. “I’m stunned, we’re stunned and you’re stunned. We’ve lost one of the best human beings ever to walk the planet, Tom Jackson. I was fortunate to work side by side with Tom for 30 years, primarily on NFL Primetime and Sunday NFL Countdown . It was a labor of love for our whole team, both in front of the camera and behind it. We always hoped our viewers enjoyed the shows as much as we did bringing it to them every week.”

Jackson is a member of the Broncos’ Ring of Fame, the franchise’s 50th anniversary team, and the Louisville Ring of Honor. He received the Pete Rozelle Radio-Television Award from the Hall of Fame in 2015.

The recent changes to the Pro Football Hall of Fame’s rules could make Jackson a candidate for the expanded “contributor” category, given that it allows former players to enhance their standing with other contributions to the game. Few have combined an impactful and prolonged playing career with an impactful and prolonged broadcasting career.

We extend our condolences to Jackson’s friends, family, teammates, and colleagues.

sports.title: Troy Aikman's latest comments invite speculation that he's hoping for an early exit
sports.summary: In isolation, the latest comments from ESPN's Troy Aikman about Monday night partner Joe Buck would have barely been noticed.
sports.body:
Aikman’s crack that Buck “ always wanted a one-man booth ” and the snark-oozing observation that Buck is “ubiquitous” happened two days after their mutual boss, ESPN president Jimmy Pitaro, called the media coverage of the Aikman-Buck feud “ disappointing .”

That was a clear message to the folks in position to add fuel to the fire: Knock it off. Aikman, in his first opportunity to speak publicly during a weekly Thursday radio segment on 96.7 The Ticket in Dallas, sprayed lighter fluid on it.

The development has sparked an uptick in speculation that Aikman will be gone not after the upcoming Super Bowl, but before it. The real question, as we see it, is whether that’s what Aikman wants.

If he knows it’s done after the Super Bowl, why delay? And if he can say just enough to get ESPN to choose to take the cringe out of an awkward kitchen — but not so much to be fired for cause — he gets the rest of the year off, with full pay.

Given that Aikman has well-documented aspirations to work for a team, why be tied to ESPN through Valentine’s Day? If ESPN tells him to take the rest of the year off, he can immediately start looking for a landing spot in a front office.

Sure, Aikman would be giving up the chance to call a Super Bowl. But he has already called six of them. And this one will play out with increasing chatter about his future, making the perfunctory ESPN press conference during Super Bowl week a standing-room event with endless questions about the Aikman-Buck relationship and Aikman’s next step.

For now, everyone will be watching and waiting. On Monday night, Aikman and Buck will be back in the booth together. Will Buck make reference to the “one-man booth” remark? If so, will Aikman take the bait?

With seven Monday night games and a wild-card broadcast to go, there will be plenty of chances for the simmer to become a boil during a broadcast. The closer it comes to happening, the more inclined ESPN may be to give Aikman what he possibly wants.

sports.title: Tyler Shough is the Saints' leading rusher, with 187 yards this season
sports.summary: As Saints quarterback Tyler Shough struggles through his second season, a good running attack could help take some pressure off him.
sports.body:
That might be OK if running the ball were Shough’s strong suit, but he has just 187 yards rushing this season. Shough is the leading rusher in New Orleans because the Saints haven’t found a running back who can establish himself as a consistent threat running the ball, not because he’s doing anything special himself.

The Saints have given five different running backs a significant number of carries this season, but none has emerged as the lead back: Alvin Kamara has 49 carries for 161 yards. Every other team in the NFL has at least one running back with more rushing yards than Kamara, the Saints’ leader. Most teams have two or more. For the Saints, relying on Shough to be their leading rusher is not a successful way to run an offense.

sports.title: Report: Daniel Jones is likely to wait to sign with the "right team at the right time"
sports.summary: New reporting doesn't mention the path he took in 2024 — signing with a practice squad.
sports.body:
And so he’ll become a free agent, like he did after he was benched (for financial reasons) and then cut by the Giants two years ago today.

Via ESPNFL, Jones is “unlikely” to sign with another team immediately. His preference, per the report, will be to “wait for the right opportunity with the right team at the right time .”

There’s a cake-and-eat-it option not mentioned by the new report. Jones can sign with a practice squad, giving him the flexibility to jump to another team’s active roster in the event the planets align for Jones to step in and play for a contender in relevant late-season games.

That’s what he did in 2024, joining the Minnesota practice squad while keeping the ability to jump to a 53-man roster elsewhere.

Why wouldn’t he do that again? It would keep him working within the confines of an NFL team, which could result in reports that he’s looking much better there than he did during his 2026 season in Indianapolis, which had him dead last among all qualifying quarterbacks with a passer rating of 65.4.

Whether he chooses to do that or not, it becomes an obvious (if not likely) option for Jones. Especially since he did the exact same thing the last time he found himself benched and then released.

sports.title: The Colts, as expected, won't activate WR Alec Pierce from injured reserve
sports.summary: As the Colts fully embrace the making of business decisions over the pursuit of victories, this one is no surprise.
sports.body:
Via Ian Rapoport of ESPNFL, the Colts won’t activate receiver Alec Pierce from injured reserve. He’ll miss the rest of the season, with the goal of being fully and completely healthy for 2027.

The situation with Pierce becomes just another one of the tangible examples of the manner in which everything has gone sideways for the Colts over the past calendar year, starting with the November 2025 trade for cornerback Sauce Gardner. Despite knowing that Pierce had an ankle issue that would eventually require surgery , the Colts re-signed Pierce at the outset of free agency to a four-year deal with an annual average of $28.5 million.

While well below the top of the market at the position, it was a major investment in a player with a significant injury. Pierce had surgery in late March and played two games in September (catching five passes for 72 yards) before landing on injured reserve due to an aggravation of the condition.

Given the timing of the deal with Pierce (it was announced just as the March 9 negotiating window opened), it appears that the Colts put a number on the table aimed at keeping him from taking a comparable deal elsewhere. With the Colts promptly trading receiver Michael Pittman Jr. to the Steelers, and in light of the limited production they’ve gotten from Pierce this year, it’s very easy to conclude they should have let Pierce walk, keeping Pittman and moving on.

At this point, with the team at 3-8 and pivoting to quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr., there’s no reason to rush Pierce back. From the moment the Colts traded guard Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner back to the 49ers, the Colts threw in the shoe on 2026. Everything that has happened since then serves only to highlight the fact that they no longer care about 2026 (to the delight of the Jets, who hold Indy’s first-round pick next year), and that they’re trying to best position themselves for 2027.

Keeping Pierce on IR is just another obvious aspect of that broader plan. And it bolsters the possibility that owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon will decide to give coach Shane Steichen another year .

After a hard-fought Week 7 game at Minnesota saw a potential 3-4 record slip to 2-5, the “we’ll get ‘em next year” plan was fully activated. While Steichen can be held accountable for the first seven games, it’s hard to pin much blame on him for the final ten.

sports.title: Steelers try for first win in Philadelphia since LBJ was president
sports.summary: October 24, 1965.
sports.body:
That’s the last time the Pittsburgh Steelers won a regular-season game in Philadelphia.

LBJ was president. Bonanza was the top show on TV. Yesterday was the No. 1 song.

The Steelers entered that game 0-5. The Eagles were 2-3. Pittsburgh’s quarterback was Bill Nelsen. Philly’s was Jack Concannon.

The 20-14 final score was fueled by a pair of defensive scores. Willie Daniel returned a fumble 17 yards for a touchdown. Jim Bradshaw had an 82-yard interception return for another six. (He had three interceptions in the game.)

The Eagles otherwise dominated. They gained 388 yards. The Steelers gained 132. Pittsburgh fumbled five times, but recovered four of them. Running back Dick Hoak, who passed away recently , led Pittsburgh with 46 yards from scrimmage.

Since that day, the Eagles are 11-0 at home against the Steelers. Today, in a game that was flexed out of the 4:25 p.m. ET window because the Eagles are in a soft-tank free fall, the Steelers are 6-3 and the Eagles are 2-7.

For the Steelers, a loss today could see 6-3 become 6-7 quickly; their next three games are against the Broncos, the Texans, and the Jaguars.

So beyond ending a 61-year streak of futility in Philly, the Steelers need to win this one today. Even if they do, those next three games could alter the trajectory of the season and throw the Steelers into a scramble for a playoff berth in a stretch run that includes the Ravens, Panthers, Titans, and Ravens.

I’ll be the first to mention that teams are not always
sports.body: It’s like each week there’s arisen a new narrative about this Buffalo Bills team. Leading into Week 11 against the Dolphins, it was all about strength of schedule… probably because of Buffalo’s competition — or lack thereof — since the bye week. I’ll be the first to mention that teams are not always what their record says they are. But what these Bills are doing is subtly different from previous Bills teams during the Josh Allen era. What has remained the same is Buffalo’s regular-season dominance. Since 2020, the Bills have been the NFL’s best team in the regular season. They have the most wins and the highest point differential by an insane margin. But like I wrote a week ago, the Sean McDermott clubs always had an uncharacteristic stumble or two during said regular season that kept them away out of the No. 1 seat in the AFC playoffs. Of course today, against the Dolphins, represents one of those “stumble” possibilities with the colossal clash on Thanksgiving against the Chiefs looming. But that’s the not the crux of this column. Are the Bills the best 8-1 team in NFL history? No. Are they the best 8-1 team in the past decade. No. But they’ve done exactly what a team should do against the competition level it has faced. Regarding the aforementioned point differential, it’s my absolute favorite measure of team quality… because it’s straightforward and pretty darn predictive. How’s this for point differential’s stickiness — 11 of the past 12 Super Bowl winners finished the regular season in the Top 6 in point differential. Insane, right? From 2004 - 2025, 17 of 22 of the clubs that hoisted the Lombardi Trophy at season’s end were a Top 6 point-differential team during the regular season. And this Bills team enters this AFC East game against the Dolphins second in point differential, at +88. If Buffalo had been squeaking by lesser opponents regularly, I’d be the first to write their 8-1 feels phony. That hasn’t been the case whatsoever. Among the nine teams at 7-2 or better right now, only the Broncos (.583) and Vikings (.518) have faced a cumulative opponent win percentage above .500. sports.title: Josh Allen is one score away from four straight seasons with 12 or more rushing touchdowns
sports.summary: Bills quarterback Josh Allen has become something that few quarterbacks are — a rushing-touchdown machine.
sports.body:
In nine 2026 games, Allen has 11 rushing touchdowns. With only one more, he’ll have his fourth straight season with 12 or more rushing touchdowns.

Via NBC Sports research, that would make him only the fifth player in NFL history to have four straight seasons with 12 or more rushing touchdowns.

The others were all running backs. LaDainian Tomlinson did it six times. Shaun Alexander accomplished it five times. Derrick Henry and Adrian Peterson did it four times each.

Henry, who has 10 this year, is two short of running his own streak to five seasons in a row.

Allen’s next rushing touchdown will give him 91 for his career, putting him in a tie for 12th all time with Franco Harris and Jerome Bettis. Given that Allen is only in his ninth season, the all-time rushing-touchdown record of 164, held my Emmitt Smith, could eventually be in jeopardy.

Three weeks in, 21 chapters are available. The full menu is here , with a button at the bottom of each chapter to quickly move to the next.

The chapters are short. Which means there are plenty of them. But each one reads quickly and, ideally, tempts the reader to read the next one.

It’s the writer’s job to make the reader want to do that. If you haven’t started, here’s Chapter One . If you like it, click to Chapter Two .

sports.title: After loss to Virginia, Bill Belichick's bowl hopes come down to NC State game

sports.title: Knee surgery complicates Puka Nacua's future
sports.summary: Timeline for recovery make mean he won't be 100 percent before free agency.
sports.body:
Via ESPN, the recovery time following surgery to repair the MCL tear is four to five months . If accurate, that ends Nacua’s 2026 season.

The problem becomes 2027. Nacua is in the last year of his rookie contract. He hasn’t gotten a second deal, due in large part to the off-field issues that recently resulted in a three-game suspension under the Personal Conduct Policy and that culminated in an offseason stay at an in-patient holistic rehab facility after he was “ drowning myself ” in alcohol.

Based on the ESPN report, Nacua won’t be back to 100 percent before free agency starts. The Rams will have to decide whether to sign him to a new deal, to apply the franchise tag (or the transition tag), or to let him become a free agent.

The injury makes it very difficult for Nacua to land in the Jaxon Smith-Njigba ballpark ($42.15 million per year), even though Nacua’s skills and abilities justify that type of deal.

The situation becomes a prime example of the extent to which off-field issues can complicate a player’s financial interests. Without the New Year’s Eve incident that resulted in a lawsuit and, eventually, a diversion program and, inevitably, a suspension under the Personal Conduct Policy, Nacua would have had his second contract by now. Or, at a minimum, he would have had greater standing to hold out (or hold in) until he got paid what he deserves.

Instead, Nacua continued to carry the injury risk into the final year of his rookie contract. And the injury risk became reality 13 days ago, when McVay dialed up a running play to Nacua on third and 11 while trying to run out the clock in a 20-13 game against the Commanders.

It’s a win for the Rams, who may be able to keep Nacua for a lot less than it would cost to give him a market-level contract. However the Rams play the situation, Nacua’s knee injury will make it easier, and cheaper, to re-sign him.

Ultimately, Nacua may have to prove in 2027 that he is back to full strength. And he may have to get through a full season unscathed to unlock the long-term deal his performances earned — but his off-field complications squandered.

sports.title: NFC North continues its historic dominance
sports.summary: They're 27-10 overall, and 21-4 in games outside the division.
sports.body:
Three of the teams (Lions, Bears, Vikings) have a record of 7-2 through 10 weeks. The Packers are 6-4.

The combined record of 27-10 equates to a success rate of 73 percent — the highest by any division through Week 10 in NFL history.

Outside the division, the teams of the NFC North are 21-4. The 84-percent success rate is the most for any division through Week 10 since the AFL-NFL merger.

This weekend, the Lions host the Bucs, the Bears host the Saints, and the Vikings face the 49ers in Mexico City.

In theory, all four teams could make the playoffs. That would require the fourth-place team landing higher in the standings than the second-place team in each of the other three divisions.

And that makes Wednesday night’s game between the 6-4 Packers and 6-4 Rams critical to the outcome of the chase for the wild-card berths in the NFC.

sports.title: Aidan Hutchinson wasn't fined for sack that injured Drake Maye
sports.summary: As expected, Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson wasn't fined for the tackle that may have ended Patriots quarterback Drake Maye's season.
sports.body:
The weekly announcement from the league includes no fines against Hutchinson.

A question emerged as to whether Hutchinson’s sack of Maye amounted to a hip-drop tackle. During the broadcast, Fox rules analyst (and former NFL senior V.P. of officiating) Mike Pereira said it wasn’t a hip-drop tackle. On Monday, NFL in-house rules analyst Walt Anderson confirmed that it wasn’t a hip-drop tackle .

But it’s not Anderson who makes the decisions on fines. Jon Runyan makes those decisions. Not surprisingly, Runyan decided that the tackle was not a violation of the rules.

Under the rules, a hip-drop tackle happens when a player “grabs the runner with one or both hands or wraps the runner with both arms; and . . . unweights himself by swiveling and dropping his hips and/or lower body, landing on and/or trapping the runner’s leg(s) at or below the knee.” Anderson said Hutchinson did not “unweight” himself or “swivel.”

Hutchinson suffered a torn ACL in his knee while celebrating the sack. Although it’s not clear whether Maye will play again in 2026, Hutchinson is done for the year.

sports.title: CeeDee Lamb fined $23,882 for block the league used as a highlight
sports.summary: Lamb was praised for the block by the league's website and by Tom Brady, but the disciplinary process said he used his helmet.
sports.body:
“Can’t-Miss Play: CeeDee Lamb’s HUGE block springs Pickens free for 39-yard TD,” the caption on the highlight video says.

Calling the play on Fox, Tom Brady praised Lamb, immediately recognizing it as a great downfield block.

But the league’s disciplinary process didn’t think it was so great. Lamb has been fined $23,882 for what the NFL deemed “Unnecessary Roughness: Use of the helmet.”

Lamb confirmed to reporters on Thursday that he had been informed he was getting fined, but he insisted he didn’t make contact with his helmet and found it frustrating that receivers take hits routinely but get fined when they make one.

“I can block, and I’m real good at doing things like that, but I get fined,” Lamb said. “I never touched him with my helmet. . . . I guess as a receiver, we can get hit, but can’t deliver the punishment.”

Lamb will surely appeal the fine for what looked, both to the league’s website and the league’s all-time greatest player, like a good block.

Thompson, 32, played in 12 regular-season games for Buffalo last season, starting 6. He totaled 5
sports.body: Grappling with injuries on defense, the Buffalo Bills have elevated linebacker Shaq Thompson and cornerback Tre’Davious White from their practice squad ahead of Sunday’s matchup with the Miami Dolphins. [Media: https://twitter.com/SalSports/status/2124255025832562722?a=XSKVjMjfw1qXVM1Adj0&s=20] Thompson, 32, played in 12 regular-season games for Buffalo last season, starting 6. He totaled 56 tackles, 1 sack, 6 tackles for loss, 2 pass breakups, and 1 fumble recovery. In Buffalo’s two playoff games, Thompson was excellent, notching 13 total tackles, a team-high 10 solo tackles, 2 tackles for loss, and an interception. The veteran is a former first-round pick of the Carolina Panthers, having been the No. 25 overall selection in the 2015 NFL Draft. Thompson will have a role this week in place of Dorian Williams, who is out with a calf injury that he suffered late in last week’s win over the New York Jets. Whether Thompson plays a significant role on defense or not is yet to be determined, but at worst, he provides strong depth for the Bills. Rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr is the other likely option to start next to Terrel Bernard. White, 31, also spent last season with the Bills. He played a significant part in the team’s defense, starting 16 games in the regular season across from Christian Benford. It’s thanks to Benford’s injured groin that White finds himself elevated this week, as he’ll either start across from rookie Davison Igbinosun or serve as depth behind the second-year man that he started over last season, Maxwell Hairston. During the 2025 season, White totaled 40 tackles, 10 pass breakups, and an interception. In the postseason, White started both games, totaling six tackles and three pass breakups. White originally entered the NFL in 2017 as Buffalo’s first-round draft choice that year, and after spending the 2024 season with the Baltimore Ravens and Los Angeles Rams, he returned home and played well last season. White allowed just 51% of the pass thrown when he was the closest man in coverage to be completed, holding opposing quarterbacks to a 71.1 quarterback rating when targeting him. The Bills and Dolphins are a 1 p.m. EDT start on Sunday. Each team’s official inactive lists will be released 90 minutes prior to kickoff.

sports.body: The injuries continue piling up for the Buffalo Bills ahead of their Week 11 home game against the Miami Dolphins. A surprise report originating from the team on Saturday afternoon revealed that Bills starting defensive tackle Ed Oliver is dealing with an oblique injury. That report comes a day after the final injury report of Week 11 (Friday’s news) that lists game-day designations, and on a day when the team didn’t practice. Oliver is now listed as questionable for Sunday’s home game, though the news is not all doom and gloom. Matt Parrino provided some context to Oliver’s injury, tweeting that “(p)er a league source, Ed Oliver notified Bills training staff this morning that he felt pain in his oblique. The staff checked it out and there’s optimism that he’ll play against the Dolphins.” Per NFL rules, Oliver’s ailment must be accounted for on the injury report even at this late stage, which is why he’s being listed as questionable. In the past, Oliver’s situation would have likely had him tabbed as “probable” for game day. The NFL has since done away with that injury designation, which has seen the questionable term pick up the slack in filing injuries throughout the league. Should Oliver be unable to go (or limited in some fashion) it would be a huge blow to Buffalo’s defense, which already has to account for injuries to starters in cornerback Christian Benford and inside linebacker Dorian Williams. Both Bills defenders have been ruled out ahead of Week 11.

I figured the Jets hadn’t been to SoFi too often, but I was shocked to learn that they haven’t been there since two trips in 2020. We all remember this as the game that shifted the Jets’ odds of having the first overall pick when every poor fanbase was looking to ‘Tank For Trevor’. The Jets won the following week and finished 2-14, securing the second overall pick and failing to properly tank. sports.body: The last time the Jets beat the Chargers, they were still representing San Diego and Plaxico Burress scored three touchdowns. Since that time, New York have lost five straight times to them, including a 27-6 drubbing in their most recent meeting in 2023. Let’s break down the Chargers’ roster going position by position: Quarterbacks Justin Herbert was a pro bowler last season, but he’s having a rough year in 2026, with career-worst numbers in almost every category. In his first six seasons, he averaged 27 touchdown passes and 11 interceptions per year. However, over halfway through the 2026 season, he has thrown for just six touchdown passes and already has 11 interceptions. He didn’t have a very productive game as a passer against the Ravens on Monday night, but at least he managed not to throw an interception for the first time all year as the Chargers finally won their first game to improve to 1-8. He also rushed for a season-high 51 yards and a touchdown. DJ Uiagalelei is the backup but he’s completed just two NFL passes in his career. Offensive Line Incredibly, five of the Chargers’ eight active offensive linemen are rookies, although this is hardly by design. They have five offensive linemen on injured reserve, including well known names like Rashawn Slater, Tyler Biadasz, Trevor Penning and Trey Pipkins. Pipkins was activated for practice last week, though, so his return is possible on Sunday. His official game status is questionable. Unsurprisingly, this has led to the Chargers struggling to protect Herbert, who has been sacked 33 times. Only Deshaun Watson has been sacked more often that that this season. The only two players to start every game so far have been second round rookie Jake Slaughter at center and veteran right guard Cole Strange.
